derivation: middle voice of apparently a prolonged form of an obsolete primary (compare G3735 (ὄρος));
def: to stretch oneself, i.e. reach out after (long for)

occurrences.text: This is a true saying, If a man desire the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work.
For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.
But now they desire a better country, that is, an heavenly: wherefore God is not ashamed to be called their God: for he hath prepared for them a city.

source: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890) and Concise Dictionaries (1894), public domain; JSON by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA).
